text:
alex: FYI, noticed SCIM provisioning to acme-corp started failing right after their IdP root cert rotation. They rotated last night at ~02:10 UTC and we see errors from the SCIM worker since then.
sana: ugh. error logs?
alex: paste from scim-worker.log: 
```
2026-11-04T02:14:03Z ERROR scim-worker decryption failed for assertion id=3f2b: XMLCipherException: Decrypt failed: AWS KMS Decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException: ciphertext has invalid key-vsn or encryption-context mismatch
stack: .../crypto/kms_client.go:112
```
chris: encryption-context mismatch -> likely KMS key policy or alias changed during cert roll? but why tied to IdP cert rotation?
maria: maybe the IdP re-encrypted the SAML artifact with a new key or changed NameID format which altered the SCIM payload signature metadata. Could be we’re failing to verify or decrypt metadata.
dom: quick check: were any KMS aliases rotated around that time? @oncall-bot can you show recent kms:Decrypt failures for key alias/riw-scim?
oncall-bot: Recent events for alias/aws/scim-key: 02:12 UTC - 12 failures (InvalidCiphertextException), 02:13 UTC - 9 failures. No CreateKey/DeleteKey events logged in same window.
sana: interesting. If no key rotation, maybe the encryption context our code sends changed because NameID format or subject confirmation changed after IdP rotation. That would produce InvalidCiphertext because KMS uses the exact encryption context for decrypt.
achieves: can we dump the incoming SAML assertion metadata (redact PII) to confirm?
chris: asked acme-corp to send their new Metadata XML. they replied with metadata.xml and log snippet showing they rotated cert chain only. No KMS key changes on their side.
maria: two immediate mitigations: 1) re-add old IdP cert to SP truststore (we accept either cert for validation) 2) update our SCIM consumer to loosen encryption-context usage fallback (short-term)
dom: can we do 1 without breaking audit/compliance? adding old cert is allowed for 48 hours under emergency ops, but must be logged + ticketed.
sana: agree. Also need audit trail: check our audit-logs for any exported keys or leaked contexts. If logs include full ciphertext or key IDs in plain text that's sensitive — escalate to vuln-triage.
acher: quick sanity check: are RBAC mappings affected? I see a customer report that admin roles weren't provisioned. Could be NameID -> email mapping changed (NameID format switched from emailAddress to transient).
chris: yep saw that in the metadata diff: <NameIDFormat>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress</NameIDFormat> -> <NameIDFormat>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient</NameIDFormat>. That breaks our attribute->role mapping.
maria: track two streams: 1) restore provisioning flow (cert fallback + KMS decrypt fix) 2) mapping fix for NameID (update mapping rules and re-run provisioning).
dom: I'll open an incident ticket and run the emergency rollback for cert truststore.
jira-bot: Created INC-3287: "SCIM provisioning failure for acme-corp after IdP cert rotation" assigned to dom, priority P1. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3287
sana: postmortem checklist: include audit logs, exact KMS request/response IDs (redact ciphertext), timeline, customer metadata a/diff, and remediation steps.
achris: mitigation applied: rolled old cert into truststore and restarted scim-worker at 02:45 UTC. Flow resumed for 78 of 120 pending users; remaining 42 require manual reconcile due to NameID format mismatch.
maria: created a short playbook for ops: 
1) if IdP rotates cert -> verify metadata issued by IdP matches SP config; accept old cert temporarily if immediate failures.
2) check KMS Decrypt errors for InvalidCiphertextException -> compare encryption context used during Encrypt/Decrypt.
3) if NameID format changed -> contact customer and update mapping; schedule a one-off resync.
sana: for vuln triage: no secrets in plaintext were found in logs. KMS key policy unchanged. Adding old cert is fine but we should require customer rotate back to emailNameID or confirm attribute mapping.
dom: closing loop with acme: they confirmed they'd switch NameID back to emailAddress in a maintenance window tomorrow and will re-run provisioning.
achris: follow-up: we'll add a probe to detect NameID format drift and alert at high-severity next time.
maria: thanks team. I'll add remediation notes to INC-3287 and mark this incident as mitigated. :thumbsup:
